examples.name: Counter-sample — 4x
paragraphs: The page starts straight into data rows with no header row. Column meaning has to be inferred from the values, which is the edge of the relation test: repeated records under one schema still make it a table, and the output MUST NOT invent the missing header row.

examples.name: Counter-sample — two-column author biographies
paragraphs: Two columns, each with bold labels — Name:, Affiliation:, Address:, Main Works: — and values beneath them, separated by horizontal rules top and bottom. Every visual cue says table: aligned label column, ruled boundaries, repeated schema across the two halves.

It is not one. The two columns are independent biographies, not two records of one relation, and the rule lines are section dividers rather than a grid. Reading it as a table would pair Marcus Ainsley with Priya Delacroix as though they shared a row.

The label/value blocks inside each column are ungridded key-value content — see Forms and Key-Value Regions§10.1 — and the bulleted publication lists are ordinary lists. The columns are unrolled in reading order, left biography first.
